feature: Webhooks (#1597) — the real Webhooks page in artifacts/portal, wired to the already-built webhooks.ts endpoints (docs/webhooks-contract-pack.md). Real design landed in Design/portal/design_handoff_full_site/screens/Webhooks.dc.html; page lives at artifacts/portal/src/pages/webhooks.tsx, route /webhooks. Design's own copy (and sync-record.md:64) settle #3523's own decision ask: 'Reveal' is dropped — the full secret is shown only once, at creation and at rotation.
notes: shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree — these assertions only go green once this session's commit is deployed by the dev-server rebuild.

apiTests prove the real, already-built backend contract directly, in the same order the page itself calls it: create (full secret returned once), list (secretPrefix only), toggle isActive via PATCH, rotate-secret (new secret returned once, old one gone), deliveries (empty for a fresh endpoint), then delete (cleanup — this run creates one real row and removes it again so it never lingers against a real test account).

ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD — the same CustomerUser testbed account test-manifests/portal/customer-home-landing.json already uses. requireAuth + resolveOwner() (webhooks.ts:71-97) scope every call to the caller's own customerId; no separate role/tenant fixture is needed.

TEST3 creates a real webhook with eventTypes ['auth.login'] (a real, always-present canonical EVENT_TYPES member, not one of the design's own illustrative/dead ones) and asserts the response carries the full plaintext 'secret' field (webhooks.ts:193) exactly once — this is the create-moment reveal the page's secret modal is built on.

TEST4 asserts the list endpoint (GET /api/portal/webhooks) never re-exposes that secret — only secretPrefix — proving the page's 'no reveal after creation' copy matches the real wire contract, not just the design's own claim.
TEST8 (DELETE) is the manifest's own cleanup step — it always runs, keeping this a repeatable, non-accumulating test run against a real account.

UI steps deliberately CANCEL rather than submit the create form (webhooks-cancel-create, not -form-submit) — the real create/secret-modal/rotate/delete round trip is already proven end to end by apiTests TEST3-TEST8 above, including its own cleanup; a UI run that also created a row would leave a second, UI-only row behind on every repeated run with no matching cleanup path from this side. Rendering + interactivity of the create form is proven here without persisting anything.

apiTests.name: SETUP — log in as the CustomerUser testbed account; extract the bearer.
TEST1 — GET /api/portal/webhooks/event-types returns the real, live SUBSCRIBABLE_EVENT_TYPES catalog.
TEST2 — GET /api/portal/webhooks lists (possibly empty) real rows, never a fixture.
TEST3 — POST creates a real webhook and returns the full plaintext secret exactly once (webhooks.ts:193).
TEST4 — GET single webhook never re-exposes the secret — only secretPrefix (webhooks.ts:219-230).
TEST5 — PATCH pauses the endpoint (isActive: false), matching the page's DELIVERING toggle.
TEST6 — POST rotate-secret returns a NEW plaintext secret, once, matching the page's rotate modal.
TEST7 — GET deliveries for the brand-new endpoint is a real, honest empty array (never delivered).
TEST8 — CLEANUP: DELETE removes the test webhook so this run leaves nothing behind on a real account.

UI7 — the submit button is now enabled (real client-side http/https + label validation, never submitted).
